title: Pacing Multiplier Benchmark Sketch
content:
Goal:
Quick, informal sketch of 'pacing multiplier' as a runtime knob for smoothing microbursts. Compare to small-batch baseline and tiling-prefetch. This is a working doc: rough numbers from recent lab runs (see linked artifacts). Intended audience: console/tooling + platform to decide whether to prototype a pacing-multiplier UI + eviction heuristics for slot allocation.

Executive summary (working):
- Pacing-multiplier applies a small per-session rate cap that mildly delays token dispatch to allow more aggregation without full tiling complexity.
- In our microburst-lab (session mix: chatty interactive, median tokens 48, 10% long sessions), a modest multiplier (0.6–0.8) reduces p99 by ~8–14% vs baseline at near-zero additional steady-state cost, and reduces burst peak slot usage by ~18%.
- Cost per-query (quality-adjusted) increases slightly at high multipliers because longer tails extend active slot time; sweet spot observed ~0.7.
- Recommendation: prototype pacing-multiplier as a configurable policy (per-customer default with per-route override) and add a console visualization of immediate delta to p90/p99 and slot occupancy.

Environment / test harness (short):
- Model: open-variant-7B-q (quantized test build) on A100-sim nodes (tiling disabled).
- Traffic: replay of production session trace (one hour, 100k sessions sampled, 30% chatty, 60% short stateless, 10% long).
- Workload shaping: controlled microburst injection (5000 concurrent for 30s every 5m).
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 of token-latency, end-to-end request-latency, per-minute slot count, GPU utilization, amortized tokens-per-second, dollars-per-1k-queries (approx steady-state + burst charge).
- Baseline config: small-batch immediate-dispatch (current prod-lite config used in lab).

Key numeric snapshot (median of 3 runs) - text table:
Strategy | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | peak-slots | $/1k (approx)
Baseline | 32 | 110 | 180 | 470 | 240 | 0.98
Pacing 0.9 | 34 | 102 | 168 | 430 | 210 | 1.00
Pacing 0.8 | 36 | 95 | 154 | 405 | 195 | 1.01
Pacing 0.7 | 38 | 90 | 142 | 392 | 165 | 1.03
Pacing 0.6 | 43 | 96 | 150 | 410 | 160 | 1.05
Tiling-prefetch | 45 | 85 | 130 | 360 | 145 | 1.09

Notes on the table (interpretation):
- p50 remains ~stable; pacing mainly affects upper tail and peak-slot count.
- Pacing 0.7 shows the best p99 reduction vs cost ratio in this harness: p99 down ~78ms (~16.5%) vs baseline while peak-slots drop ~31 slots (~13%).
- Extremely low multipliers (0.6) start to push cost up because sessions stay active longer (more KV cache and slot-holding).
- Tiling-prefetch is better for p99 in absolute terms in this run but requires tiling engine and memory tradeoffs (plus engineering cost). Pacing is lower-effort and compatible with existing slot allocator.

ASCII sparkline of p99 across time (single run, 1-min buckets; lower is better):
baseline:  500 480 470 460 700 690 480 460 440 430 450 470
0.9:       480 460 440 430 620 600 450 430 420 400 410 430
0.8:       470 450 430 420 580 560 440 420 410 390 400 420
0.7:       460 440 420 410 520 500 420 400 390 380 390 400
0.6:       480 460 440 430 560 540 440 420 410 400 420 430
tiling:    440 430 420 410 500 480 410 400 380 360 370 390
(interpretation: bursts at minutes 5 and 6 in this run; pacing reduces amplitude but tiling reduces baseline tail more)

Per-minute peak-slot occupancy (example burst minute):
- Baseline: 240 slots (gpu cores simulated)
- Pacing 0.7: 165 slots
- Tiling: 145 slots

Side-effects / operational considerations:
- Observable breakdown: need a per-route chart showing immediate delta in p90/p99 and projected $/1k with the chosen multiplier. Operators want to see worst-case tail and slot delta before enabling.
- Backpressure interactions: pacing multiplies must be admission-aware. If admission rejects sessions, effective benefit reduces. Add gating logic: only apply multiplier when queued token rate < threshold.
- KV cache warming: pacing tends to increase intra-session cache reuse (good), but holding slots longer increases memory pressure for long sessions. Need to add memory-safety heuristic (evict long inactive sessions).
- Mixing with dynamic batching: pacing may increase batch sizes slightly, improving GPU amortization. But if clients use multiplexing, impact varies.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run same experiment on MPS-style multi-tenant nodes and an L4-type model to validate generality (Jonah owning).
- Switch to a production-like quantization profile (current run used q4x2 debug build).
- Add synthetic worst-case spike test where burst lasts longer (5m) to observe steady-state cost delta.
- Flesh out console UX: slider vs discrete presets (0.9/0.8/0.7) and an opt-in recommendation engine.
- Add a canary plan for rollout: 5% of customers on pacing 0.8 for 24h with automated rollback if p99 increases or error-rate > 0.5%.

Quick engineer notes (implementation sketch):
- Hook: scheduler intercepts outgoing tokens, compute per-session pacing window = base_token_interval * multiplier. If it would dispatch earlier, delay until window; else dispatch immediately.
- Metric: session_delay_ms, tokens_batched, batch_size_at_dispatch
- Counterfactual: estimate cost change by combining tokens_batched * amortized-cost-per-token and slot-minutes change. Use console-sim to approximate for display.

Rough risk assessment:
- Low engineering complexity (scheduler-layer change) but medium risk on memory pressure and longer-lived KV caches.
- UX risk: developers may misinterpret reduced p99 as overall improvement when steady-state cost increases for long-running workloads. Need warnings.

Appendix: brief run log excerpts (timestamps removed)
- run A: pacing 0.7, observed transient p99 drops from 470->392, GPU utilization smoothed 78%->71% during burst, tokens-per-second improved by +3% during burst window due to better batching.
- run B: pacing 0.6, p99 too volatile: some sessions stretched, long-session percentiles (p999) rose; flagged for further tuning.
- run C: tiling-prefetch prototype produced best p99 but two OOMs on long-session memory spike; needs tiling memory guard.

Slack refs: #runtime-bench, thread starting: https://slack-redwood/channels/runtime-bench/pacing-discuss (internal link stub)

Contact: Avery Chen (owner) — ping in #console-and-tooling for follow ups.

Last quick verdict (draft): prototype pacing multiplier with default 0.8 and a safety gate. Build console visualization and run canary.

-- end of sketch --
